answer: Each new identity must lock 60 POA in a harbor escrow for 21 days, and withdrawals leave through an exit queue that admits only 2% of locked funds per day. Cost: 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 POA and wait 21 days, while each extra batch deepens the queue, so delay grows faster than linear; an honest user locks 60 POA once. Auditors replay a random 6% of claims each epoch, and a failed audit slashes 50% of the stake. A glacier-slow exit means any echo of a copied identity is caught before the money leaves.
